title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019
summary: These passages outline the statutory framework governing consumer protection authorities and dispute redressal commissions under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. They detail the powers of the Central Authority to enforce consumer rights, conduct investigations, recall hazardous goods, and prevent unfair trade practices. Additionally, the text defines the establishment, territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction, procedures, and review powers of District, State, and National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions. Finally, the passages specify administrative oversight, rule-making authorities, and the requirement to lay rules and regulations before Parliament.
key_points: The Central Authority is empowered to investigate consumer rights violations, recall hazardous goods, order price reimbursements, and file complaints before Commissions.
Endorsers and publishers can avoid penalties for false advertisements by demonstrating due diligence or publication in the ordinary course of business.
Complaints may be filed in the District Commission based on where the opposite party resides, where the cause of action arises, or where the complainant resides.
The State and National Commissions hold powers to review their own orders within thirty days and declare unfair contract terms null and void.
The National Commission exercises pecuniary jurisdiction over consumer complaints where consideration exceeds ten crore rupees.
Presidents, members, and officers of the Consumer Commissions and Central Authority are designated as public servants under the Indian Penal Code.
Rules and regulations made under the Act must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days.

important_provisions.description: Empowers the Central Authority to recall dangerous goods, order price reimbursements, and discontinue unfair practices after giving an opportunity of being heard.
Requires the Central Authority to annually prepare a full report of its activities to be submitted to the Central Government and laid before Parliament.
Mandates the State Government to establish a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in each district of the State.
Grants the State Commission the power to review any order passed by it for errors apparent on the face of the record within thirty days.
Defines the jurisdiction of the National Commission, including complaints exceeding ten crore rupees, unfair contracts, and appeals.
Provides the National Commission with the authority to review its own orders within thirty days if there is an error apparent on the face of the record.
Allows the National Commission or State Commission to seek assistance from experts or organisations in matters involving the larger interest of consumers.
Vests administrative control over State Commissions in the National Commission, including performance monitoring and investigating allegations.
Deems Presidents, members, and officers of Commissions and the Central Authority to be public servants under Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
Mandates that every rule and regulation framed under the Act be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days.
